in_english.long_meaning: The name Blaise originates from the Latin 'Blaseus,' meaning 'blazing' or 'burning.' It is associated with Saint Blaise, a 4th-century martyr who was known for his healing powers and his protection of the poor and the oppressed. In Christian tradition, Blaise is often invoked for protection and healing, and his feast day is celebrated on February 3rd. The name Blaise is also linked to the Greek word 'blazon,' meaning 'to blaze,' and the Hebrew word 'blitz,' meaning 'lightning.' In modern times, the name Blaise has been adopted in various forms, including Blaise, Blaze, and Blazey. It is suitable for parents seeking a strong and distinctive name with rich spiritual significance.

saint_reference.note: Saint Blaise was a 4th-century martyr and bishop who was known for his healing powers and his protection of the poor and the oppressed.

data.cultural_impact: Blaise is a patron saint known for his miraculous powers in healing throat ailments and physical wounds. In the Middle Ages, a tradition of carrying the bread blessed at the Feast of St. Blaise (February 3) was used as a means of protection against sore throats and other diseases. Even today, the blessing of throats on this day is practiced in various Christian denominations, particularly in the Eastern Catholic and Eastern Orthodox Churches.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Blaise evokes the image of a powerful intercessor for those who are suffering physically, especially in connection with healing and restoration. This name can serve as a reminder of our faith in God's ability to heal, comfort, and provide relief in the midst of pain and discomfort. Additionally, the association of Blaise with the throat can symbolize the importance of the power of prayer and the spoken word in our connection to God and to each other.

historical_references.reference: Blaise was a 4th century bishop of Sebaste in Cappadocia, known for his miraculous powers and his resistance to Roman persecution.

trends: Blaise is a common name in France and Quebec, Canada.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Blaise, derived from the Roman name Blasius, symbolizes healing and protection. Named after the early Christian saint, Blaise is believed to have cured a child's choking, making him the patron saint of throat ailments and hospitals. Embodying compassion and miraculous power, Blaise encourages us to offer help and healing to those in need.
